def-it-real-differential-entropy:
## Definition

If $X$ has Lebesgue density $f$ on $\mathbb R^d$ and $\int f\ln f$ is a finite real number, its differential entropy in nats is $h(X):=-\int_{\mathbb R^d}f(x)\ln f(x)\,dx$. If $(X,S)$ has conditional densities $f_{X|S=s}$ for almost every $s$ and the indicated integral is finite, set $h(X|S):=\int h(f_{X|S=s})\,dP_S(s)$. We use only these finite-integral cases; differential entropy is not defined here by a formal subtraction of possibly infinite quantities.
def-it-two-user-real-awgn-mac-code:
## Definition

Fix powers $P_1,P_2\ge0$ and noise variance $N>0$. At use $i$ the real channel is
$$Y_i=X_{1i}+X_{2i}+Z_i,$$
where the noises are independent of the messages and of one another, each with Lebesgue density $\phi_N(z)=(2\pi N)^{-1/2}e^{-z^2/(2N)}$. The Gaussian integral proves this density has mass one. A length-$n$ no-feedback code has independent uniform messages $M_j\in[M_j]$, separate deterministic encoders $f_j:[M_j]\to\mathbb R^n$, and a joint decoder $g:\mathbb R^n\to[M_1]\times[M_2]$. Write $X_j^n=f_j(M_j)$. Its average joint error is $P_e=\Pr[g(Y^n)\ne(M_1,M_2)]$ and its expected block-power constraints are $n^{-1}\sum_i\mathbb E X_{ji}^2\le P_j$, separately for $j=1,2$. The rate is $R_j=n^{-1}\ln M_j$ nats/use. Achievability means a sequence with error tending to zero and limiting lower rates at least the specified pair; the capacity region is the closure of all achievable pairs.
def-it-two-user-real-awgn-mac-feedback-c:
## Definition

Use the channel, independent messages, noise law, average joint error, powers $P_1,P_2$ and nats/use convention of [[def-it-two-user-real-awgn-mac-code]]. A length-$n$ perfect-feedback encoder for user $j$ is a deterministic family $f_{ji}:[M_j]\times\mathbb R^{i-1}\to\mathbb R$, $1\le i\le n$, with $X_{ji}=f_{ji}(M_j,Y^{i-1})$; at $i=1$ the history is the singleton empty tuple. Both senders receive the same noiseless past output, and there is no message sharing or preshared common randomness. The same expected block-power constraint is imposed.
lem-it-finite-gaussian-mixture-entropy-b:
## Statement

Let $X=(X_1,\ldots,X_d)$ be a real random vector with $\mathbb E\|X\|^2<\infty$, and let $Z$ be independent of $X$ with density $(2\pi N)^{-d/2}e^{-\|z\|^2/(2N)}$, $N>0$. Then $Y=X+Z$ has a positive density and finite differential entropy. Each coordinate satisfies $h(Y_k)\le\frac12\ln(2\pi e\,\operatorname{Var}Y_k)$, while $h(Y)\le\sum_kh(Y_k)$ and $h(Y)\ge h(Z)=\frac d2\ln(2\pi eN)$. If a side variable $S$ admits a conditional law $P_{X|S=s}$ with finite second moment almost surely, then each conditional Gaussian convolution has finite entropy and
$$h(Y\mid S)\le\frac12\ln\!\left(2\pi e\left[N+\mathbb E\operatorname{Var}(X\mid S)\right]\right).$$
def-it-physically-degraded-dm-broadcast-:
## Definition

A finite physically degraded two-receiver DM broadcast channel has finite nonempty input/output alphabets $\mathcal X,\mathcal Y_1,\mathcal Y_2$ and kernels $W_1(y_1\mid x)$ and $W_2(y_2\mid y_1)$ such that
$$W(y_1,y_2\mid x)=W_1(y_1\mid x)W_2(y_2\mid y_1).$$
Receiver 1 is called the stronger receiver. This factorization fixes a joint coupling of the outputs and gives the Markov chain $X\to Y_1\to Y_2$ for every input law. No feedback is part of this definition.
def-it-two-user-discrete-memoryless-mac:
## Definition

A two-user finite discrete memoryless multiple-access channel (DM-MAC) consists of finite nonempty input alphabets $\mathcal X_1,\mathcal X_2$, a finite nonempty output alphabet $\mathcal Y$, and a stochastic kernel $W(y\mid x_1,x_2)$ from $\mathcal X_1\times\mathcal X_2$ to $\mathcal Y$ in the convention of [[def-finite-stochastic-kernel]]. Its length-$n$ conditional law is $W^n(y^n\mid x_1^n,x_2^n)=\prod_{i=1}^nW(y_i\mid x_{1i},x_{2i})$.
lem-it-awgn-feedback-estimation-covarian:
## Statement

Let $(X_1,X_2)$ be centered jointly Gaussian with variances $P_1,P_2>0$, correlation $\rho\in[0,1)$, and let $Z\sim N(0,N)$ be independent, $N>0$. For $Y=X_1+X_2+Z$, put $D=N+P_1+P_2+2\rho\sqrt{P_1P_2}$. Then
$$\operatorname{Var}(X_1\mid Y)=\frac{P_1[N+P_2(1-\rho^2)]}{D},\quad \operatorname{Var}(X_2\mid Y)=\frac{P_2[N+P_1(1-\rho^2)]}{D},$$
$$\operatorname{Cov}(X_1-\mathbb E[X_1\mid Y],X_2-\mathbb E[X_2\mid Y])=\frac{\rho\sqrt{P_1P_2}N-P_1P_2(1-\rho^2)}{D}.$$
After scaling the two errors to variances $P_1,P_2$ and reversing the sign of the second, their correlation is
$$\rho_{\rm new}=\frac{\sqrt{P_1P_2}(1-\rho^2)-\rho N}{\sqrt{[N+P_1(1-\rho^2)][N+P_2(1-\rho^2)]}}.$$
def-it-finite-dmc-feedback-code:
## Definition

For a finite DMC $W:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ as in [[def-discrete-memoryless-channel]], a length-$n$ feedback code has a uniform message $M\in[M]$, deterministic causal encoders $f_i:[M]\times\mathcal Y^{i-1}\to\mathcal X$ and a decoder $g:\mathcal Y^n\to[M]$. The encoder at time $i$ sees only $Y^{i-1}$, sets $X_i=f_i(M,Y^{i-1})$, and the causal joint law is
$$\Pr(M=m,Y^n=y^n)=\frac1M\prod_{i=1}^n W(y_i\mid f_i(m,y^{i-1})).$$
Equivalently, at each positive-probability message-and-past-output history, $Y_i$ has conditional law $W(\cdot\mid f_i(m,y^{i-1}))$. Its average error is $\Pr[g(Y^n)\ne M]$, rate is $n^{-1}\ln M$ nats/use, and the feedback capacity is the closure of rates achievable with error tending to zero. There is no input-cost constraint.
def-it-physically-degraded-dm-broadcast-:
## Definition

For the channel of [[def-it-physically-degraded-dm-broadcast-channel]], a length-$n$ private-message code has independent uniform messages $M_1\in[M_1]$ and $M_2\in[M_2]$, a single deterministic encoder $f:[M_1]\times[M_2]\to\mathcal X^n$, and decoders $g_j:\mathcal Y_j^n\to[M_j]$. Receiver $j$ estimates only $M_j$. Average joint error is $\Pr[\widehat M_1\ne M_1\text{ or }\widehat M_2\ne M_2]$. Rates are $R_j=n^{-1}\ln M_j$ nats/use; capacity means the closure of rate pairs achievable with vanishing joint error. No feedback is present.
def-it-two-user-discrete-memoryless-mac-:
## Definition

For a DM-MAC as in [[def-it-two-user-discrete-memoryless-mac]], a length-$n$ no-feedback code consists of independent uniform private messages $M_j\in[M_j]$, separate deterministic message-only encoders $f_j:[M_j]\to\mathcal X_j^n$, and one joint decoder $g:\mathcal Y^n\to[M_1]\times[M_2]$. The average joint error is $\Pr[g(Y^n)\ne(M_1,M_2)]$; $R_j=n^{-1}\ln M_j$ nats/use. A pair is achievable if a sequence has error tending to zero and limiting lower rates at least the pair; the capacity region is the closure. In particular, independent messages and separate encoders give $X_{1i}\perp X_{2i}$ at every coordinate.

## Definition

For the finite DM-MAC of [[def-it-two-user-discrete-memoryless-mac]], a perfect-feedback length-$n$ code has independent uniform messages $M_j\in[M_j]$, deterministic encoders $f_{ji}:[M_j]\times\mathcal Y^{i-1}\to\mathcal X_j$ and a joint decoder from $\mathcal Y^n$ to the message pair. Both users see the same noiseless past output $Y^{i-1}$ before use $i$; neither sees the other user's message. Rates are $R_j=n^{-1}\ln M_j$ nats/use and error is average joint message error. Achievability means a sequence with vanishing error and limiting lower rates at least the specified pair; capacity is the closure.
lem-it-fano-for-finite-message-density-o:
## Statement

Let $M$ be uniform on a finite set of size $m\ge2$, let $S$ be finite, and suppose $Y\mid(M,S)$ has a Lebesgue density. For every measurable estimator $\widehat M=\phi(Y,S)$ with error probability $\epsilon$, define $H(M\mid Y,S):=\int H(p_{M|y,s})\,dP_{Y,S}(y,s)$ using its finite posterior vector. Then
$$H(M\mid Y,S)\le h_b(\epsilon)+\epsilon\ln(m-1)\le\ln2+\epsilon\ln m,$$
where $h_b(t)=-t\ln t-(1-t)\ln(1-t)$ and $0\ln0=0$. For $m=1$, the conditional entropy is zero.
lem-it-ozarow-feedback-sum-corner-achiev:
## Statement

Let $P_1,P_2,N>0$ and write $s_j=P_j/N$. There is a unique $\rho_\star\in(0,1)$ satisfying
$$(1+s_1(1-\rho_\star^2))(1+s_2(1-\rho_\star^2))=1+s_1+s_2+2\rho_\star\sqrt{s_1s_2}.$$
For the perfect-feedback channel of [[def-it-two-user-real-awgn-mac-feedback-code]], the rate pair
$$\left(\frac12\ln(1+s_1(1-\rho_\star^2)),\frac12\ln(1+s_2(1-\rho_\star^2))\right)$$
is achievable under the expected average-power constraints. The two rates sum to $\frac12\ln(1+s_1+s_2+2\rho_\star\sqrt{s_1s_2})$.
def-it-two-correlated-iid-sources-over-d:
## Definition

Let $(S_{1t},S_{2t})_{t\ge1}$ be the $k=2$ case of the finite IID multisource in [[def-it-finite-iid-multisource]], with finite nonempty component alphabets and common joint law $P_{S_1S_2}$. A length-$n$ lossless source-channel code over a DM-MAC as in [[def-it-two-user-discrete-memoryless-mac]] has separate deterministic encoders $f_j:\mathcal S_j^n\to\mathcal X_j^n$ and one decoder $g:\mathcal Y^n\to\mathcal S_1^n\times\mathcal S_2^n$. Its error is $\Pr[g(Y^n)\ne(S_1^n,S_2^n)]$. Reliable transmission means a sequence of such codes with error tending to zero. All source entropies are in nats and use [[def-it-finite-conditional-entropy]].
lem-it-awgn-feedback-rate-splitting-achi:
## Statement

Let $P_1,P_2,N>0$, write $C(t)=\frac12\ln(1+t)$, and let $\rho_\star$ be the unique sum-corner parameter from [[lem-it-ozarow-feedback-sum-corner-achievable]]. For every $0<\rho<\rho_\star$, the feedback channel of [[def-it-two-user-real-awgn-mac-feedback-code]] achieves, in closure, the user-1-dominant sum-rate corner
$$R_1=C\!\left(\frac{P_1(1-\rho^2)}N\right),\qquad R_2=C\!\left(\frac{P_1+P_2+2\rho\sqrt{P_1P_2}}N\right)-R_1.$$
Interchanging the user labels gives the opposite dominant corner.
thm-it-cover-leung-feedback-mac-inner-bo:
## Statement

For the two-user finite DM-MAC with perfect causal output feedback in [[def-it-two-user-discrete-memoryless-mac-feedback-code]], every nonnegative rate pair in the closure of
$$R_1<I(X_1;Y\mid X_2,U),\qquad R_2<I(X_2;Y\mid X_1,U),\qquad R_1+R_2<I(X_1,X_2;Y)$$
for some finite law $P_UP_{X_1|U}P_{X_2|U}W_{Y|X_1X_2}$ is achievable. This is an inner bound; no general feedback-capacity equality is asserted.
thm-it-two-user-real-awgn-mac-capacity-r:
## Statement

For the channel, independent private messages, average joint-error convention and expected average-power constraints in [[def-it-two-user-real-awgn-mac-code]], the capacity region in nats/use is
$$\overline{\bigcup}\left\{(R_1,R_2)\in[0,\infty)^2:\ R_1\le\frac12\ln(1+P_1/N),\ R_2\le\frac12\ln(1+P_2/N),\ R_1+R_2\le\frac12\ln(1+(P_1+P_2)/N)\right\}.$$
The overline means closure; equivalently the strict inequalities for positive-rate users are achievable and the closed displayed region is their closure. The theorem is for independent messages and separate no-feedback encoders.
lem-it-cover-elgamal-salehi-conditional-:
## Statement

Let $Q,S_1,S_2,X_1,X_2,Y$ have the finite law
$$P_QP_{S_1S_2}P_{X_1|S_1Q}P_{X_2|S_2Q}W_{Y|X_1X_2}.$$
Fix a deterministic $q^n$ and a transmitted tuple $(s_1^n,s_2^n,x_1^n,x_2^n,y^n)$ such that $(q^n,s_1^n,s_2^n,x_1^n,x_2^n,y^n)$ is support-restricted strongly typical for this law within tolerance $\delta$. For every source sequence $s_j^n$, independently generate a user-$j$ codeword with law $\prod_iP_{X_j|S_jQ}(\cdot\mid s_{ji},q_i)$; all entries and both users' codebooks are independent. A decoder tests joint typicality at tolerance $\delta$.

There is a finite constant $K$ and a function $\omega(\delta)\downarrow0$ such that the conditional expected numbers $N_1,N_2,N_{12}$ of wrong typical candidates differing in source 1 only, source 2 only, and both sources, respectively, satisfy
$$\begin{aligned} \mathbb E N_1&\le(n+1)^K e^{-n[I(X_1;Y|X_2,S_2,Q)-H(S_1|S_2)-\omega(\delta)]},\\ \mathbb E N_2&\le(n+1)^K e^{-n[I(X_2;Y|X_1,S_1,Q)-H(S_2|S_1)-\omega(\delta)]},\\ \mathbb E N_{12}&\le(n+1)^K e^{-n[I(X_1,X_2;Y|Q)-H(S_1,S_2)-\omega(\delta)]}. \end{aligned}$$
The expectations are over the unexposed wrong source-indexed codebook entries. The constants depend only on the target law and alphabets, not on the particular typical transmitted tuple.
thm-it-ozarow-awgn-mac-feedback-capacity:
## Statement

For the real two-user AWGN MAC with perfect causal common output feedback, independent private messages, average joint error and expected average-power constraints of [[def-it-two-user-real-awgn-mac-feedback-code]], the capacity region in nats/use is
$$\bigcup_{0\le\rho\le1}\left\{(R_1,R_2)\in[0,\infty)^2:\ R_j\le\frac12\ln\!\left(1+\frac{P_j(1-\rho^2)}N\right),\quad R_1+R_2\le\frac12\ln\!\left(1+\frac{P_1+P_2+2\rho\sqrt{P_1P_2}}N\right)\right\}.$$
The parameter $\rho$ is induced by causal feedback; no preshared common randomness or common message is part of the model.
thm-it-cover-el-gamal-salehi-correlated-:
## Statement

Let $(S_1,S_2)$ be finite and let its IID copies be transmitted losslessly over the DM-MAC of [[def-it-two-user-discrete-memoryless-mac]] using the separate encoders of [[def-it-two-correlated-iid-sources-over-dm-mac-code]]. If there is a finite $Q$ independent of $(S_1,S_2)$ and a law
$$P_QP_{S_1S_2}P_{X_1|S_1,Q}P_{X_2|S_2,Q}W_{Y|X_1X_2}$$
such that
$$\begin{aligned} H(S_1\mid S_2)&<I(X_1;Y\mid X_2,S_2,Q),\\ H(S_2\mid S_1)&<I(X_2;Y\mid X_1,S_1,Q),\\ H(S_1,S_2)&<I(X_1,X_2;Y\mid Q), \end{aligned}$$
then the two correlated IID sources can be transmitted with vanishing average joint error. This is a sufficient condition only; it is not a general capacity characterization for correlated sources over a DM-MAC.
thm-it-finite-dmc-feedback-does-not-incr:
## Statement

For a finite DMC $W$ without input-cost constraints, the vanishing-average-error capacity with perfect causal output feedback equals its ordinary information capacity
$$C(W)=\max_{P_X}I(P_X;W)$$
from [[def-discrete-memoryless-channel-information-capacity]]. The feedback code convention is [[def-it-finite-dmc-feedback-code]].
thm-it-physically-degraded-dm-broadcast-:
## Statement

For the private-message code of [[def-it-physically-degraded-dm-broadcast-code]] over the physically degraded channel $X\to Y_1\to Y_2$ of [[def-it-physically-degraded-dm-broadcast-channel]], the capacity region is the closure of the union over finite $U$ and laws $P_{UX}$ inducing $U\to X\to Y_1\to Y_2$ of rate pairs
$$R_1\le I(X;Y_1\mid U),\qquad R_2\le I(U;Y_2).$$
Receiver 1 is the stronger receiver and decodes only its own private message in the operational code; the auxiliary $U$ is a coding variable, not an additional message.
thm-it-two-user-discrete-memoryless-mac-:
## Statement

For the average-joint-error no-feedback code of [[def-it-two-user-discrete-memoryless-mac-code]] over the finite DM-MAC, the capacity region is the closure of the union over all finite $Q$ and laws $P_QP_{X_1|Q}P_{X_2|Q}W$ of
$$R_1\le I(X_1;Y\mid X_2,Q),\quad R_2\le I(X_2;Y\mid X_1,Q),\quad R_1+R_2\le I(X_1,X_2;Y\mid Q).$$
Here $Q$ is a public time-sharing variable independent of both private messages; conditional on each $Q=q$, the two input laws are a product. This result does not characterize maximal-error capacity.
ex-it-ozarow-awgn-mac-feedback-rate-regi:
## Statement

For $P_1=P_2=N=1$ and $\rho=1/2$, the feedback-region individual bounds are $R_j\le\frac12\ln(7/4)$ and the sum bound is $R_1+R_2\le\ln2$. The point $R_1=R_2=\frac12\ln(7/4)$ satisfies all three constraints and has sum rate strictly larger than the no-feedback sum bound $\frac12\ln3$.
ex-it-binary-xor-dm-mac-product-input-re:
## Statement

For the deterministic binary XOR channel $Y=X_1\oplus X_2$, the independent-private-message capacity region is the triangle $R_1,R_2\ge0$, $R_1+R_2\le\ln2$. Independent uniform inputs attain the maximum sum information $\ln2$. A fixed-$Q$ correlated law $X_1=X_2\sim\operatorname{Bern}(1/2)$ is not a product input law; it can be represented only by mixing deterministic product laws with a public time-sharing variable, and that common variable supplies no private-message rate conditional on $Q$.
ex-it-correlated-source-binary-adder-dm-:
## Statement

Let $(S_1,S_2)$ have probabilities $P(0,0)=P(0,1)=P(1,1)=1/3$ and $P(1,0)=0$, and let the binary-adder MAC be $Y=X_1+X_2\in\{0,1,2\}$. The uncoded source maps $X_j=S_j$ give zero-error transmission because sums $0,1,2$ correspond respectively to source pairs $(0,0),(0,1),(1,1)$. The source joint entropy is $\ln3$, while the maximum sum mutual information over independent product inputs is $\frac32\ln2<\ln3$. Thus separate lossless source descriptions followed by the independent-private-message product-input MAC region cannot carry this source pair at its joint entropy, whereas the correlated source-channel code does.
